task.title: Removing background noise
task.shortdesc: Take a noise profile from a quiet section, then apply Noise Reduction to the whole track to remove hum, hiss and fan noise.

context.p: Background noise such as hum from electronics, hiss from a microphone or fan noise degrades a recording. The Noise Reduction effect learns what the noise sounds like from a section that contains nothing else, then removes it everywhere.

step.cmd: Find a section of the recording that contains only the background noise.

info.p: Look for a quiet gap at the beginning or end. You need at least half a second of noise-only audio.

step.cmd: Choose EffectNoise Removal and RepairNoise Reduction, then click Get Noise Profile.

stepresult.p: captures the character of the noise and closes the dialog.

step.cmd: Select the whole track with Ctrl+A or Cmd+A.
Open Noise Reduction again, adjust the settings and click OK.

info.note: Too much noise reduction makes voices sound metallic or underwater. Start moderate, increase gradually, and use Preview before applying.

result.p: The background noise is reduced across the whole track. Play it back to check that the voice still sounds natural.

tasktroubleshooting.p: If the voice sounds hollow after the effect, undo, then lower Noise reduction to 6 dB and try again. If the noise is a constant hum at one pitch, the Notch Filter effect removes it with less damage to the voice.
